key_insight: Different Shapley-value formulations yield semantically distinct explanations and common quantitative benchmarks often fail to predict which explanations are actually useful to humans in high-stakes, low-latency settings.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between theoretical/benchmark evaluation of Shapley variants and real human utility by auditing multiple formulations under operational constraints to reveal mismatches between proxy metrics and human-centered usefulness.
method: Develop a unified amortized framework to compute and compare eight Shapley-value variants under consistent, low-latency operational constraints.
Isolate semantic differences across variants and run a human-centered audit in high-stakes decision scenarios to measure alignment between proxy metrics and human utility.
Quantitatively and qualitatively analyze where common benchmarks diverge from human judgments, identifying practical failure modes for deployment.
impact: Helps AI/ML practitioners choose and evaluate explanation methods based on human-centered criteria rather than benchmark scores alone, reducing risk in high-stakes, time-sensitive deployments.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic of the unified amortized pipeline highlighting where each Shapley variant differs
Bar/heatmap comparing benchmark scores vs. measured human utility for the eight variants to show mismatches
Flowchart of the human-centered audit workflow (task setup, metrics, decisions, feedback)
Icon set representing high-stakes domains (e.g., healthcare, finance) and low-latency constraints (clock/timer)
paper_title: Rethinking XAI Evaluation: A Human-Centered Audit of Shapley Benchmarks in High-Stakes Settings
paper_authors: Inês Oliveira e Silva, Sérgio Jesus, Iker Perez, Rita P. Ribeiro, Carlos Soares
